resources.string: Getting the floor alert ready… wait a moment.
It is approximate: always check the floor signs.
This phone has no barometer, so it cannot detect the floor change. When you arrive, tap \"I\'m here\".
Going down… about %1$d m so far.
Going up… about %1$d m so far.
It looks like you are now on the %1$s. Tap \"I\'m here\" to confirm.
Go down to the %1$s. I will let you know when you arrive.
Go up to the %1$s. I will let you know when you arrive.
It looks like you are going up, but you need to go down.
It looks like you are going down, but you need to go up.
Nod with the phone to open the reader: with the screen facing up, tilt the top edge towards you and back to the starting position, twice in a row.
This phone has no compatible gravity sensor or accelerometer. You can use the button.
Getting ready… hold the phone still for a moment.
The app does not store your location. It only remembers, on this phone, the last space you looked up, your name if you gave it and your bookings.

During the route, with the screen facing up, tilt the top edge of the phone towards you and back to the starting position, twice in a row. The phone vibrates and the reader opens. The \"Scan checkpoint\" button does the same.
Tap \"Listen\" or hold the phone to your ear to hear the route step or the space name. You can pause, resume or stop it. The phone volume is used.

On walking sections, hold the phone in front of you (flat or upright) and tap \"Calibrate\". The thick arrow points to where the next point is and the thin one to where you are pointing. When they match, both turn green and it says \"You are on track\"; otherwise they turn red and it tells you which way to turn. On stairs and lifts it tells you when you reach the floor. It is an aid: always check the signs.

Opens the walking route in Google Maps (Maps needs Internet). If you allow location, the GPS tells you when you reach the entrance. Inside the building GPS is not reliable: scan the entrance checkpoint to confirm you are already inside.
How to get to the ETSIIT

Choose a day, a room and a time and confirm. It is a demo: rooms and times are examples and the booking is only stored on this phone, it is not sent to the library. You can cancel it in \"My bookings\".

Choose where you are and where you want to go (and, if you like, the lift route). At each step you will see the photo taken from the point where you are and the instruction to the next one; confirm that you have arrived by reading the point\'s QR code or NFC tag, typing its code or tapping \"I am here\". The route never moves on by itself. This demo only has the route between the main entrance and classroom 2.2, there and back.
Type a name or part of the description and open its details. From the details of room 2.2 you can start the indoor route to it.
You can also hold the phone to your ear to hear it. The phone volume is used.
This phone has no proximity sensor: use the \"Listen\" button.
Reading aloud is not available on this phone (no voice for this language). The information is still on screen.
Could not calibrate: the phone compass is not giving a reliable reading. Move away from metal objects, move the phone in a figure of eight and try again.
low: move the phone in a figure of eight
unreliable: move away from metal and make a figure of eight
Test mode (long-press \"Am I on track?\" to hide it)
Hold the phone in front of you, flat or upright, and tap \"Calibrate\". You will see where the next point is.
Green: you are on track. Red: turn until they match. \"N\" marks north.
Thin arrow: where your phone is pointing.
Thick arrow: where the next point is.
There is no direction to check on this section: follow the instruction and the signs.
This phone has no orientation sensor: the direction cannot be checked. Follow the instruction and the signs.
I cannot check the direction right now. Tap \"Calibrate again\".
I\'m already at the ETSIIT: start indoor route
According to GPS you are now next to the ETSIIT entrance.
According to GPS you are %1$s from the entrance.
We will let you know when you reach the entrance.
Without location permission we cannot tell you when you arrive. Google Maps and the indoor route still work.
Location is turned off on this phone.
If you allow location, the app will use GPS while this screen is open to tell you when you reach the entrance and offer you the indoor route. Your position is not stored.
The GPS signal is weak right now. Turn on precise location or go outside so we can tell you when you arrive.
You are probably already inside the ETSIIT: the GPS signal has weakened, which is normal inside a building. GPS cannot be sure: scan the entrance checkpoint to confirm.
Google Maps needs an Internet connection to calculate the route.
There is no app to open maps on this phone.
The system settings could not be opened.
Open walking route in Google Maps
Already inside? Scan the entrance QR code or NFC tag (or type its code) to confirm and start the route from there.
That point is not part of the indoor route. Scan the entrance checkpoint.

Test data: the route, photos and plan positions are approximate and were prepared for the demo. Always check the signs in the building.
